contract: X.Org twm 1.0.13.1 session lifecycle and wtwm Wayland translation

manual.quit.text: This function causes \fItwm\fP to restore the window's borders and exit.

reference_behavior.session_owner: When twm is the foreground last client, its exit is the login-session boundary.

restart_arguments: -restore with the newly written window-state file

session_owner.model: one foreground compositor child supervised by the login manager

order: parse and validate the complete configuration
resolve and optionally load compositor-owned saved state
create display, backend, protocols, and input state
publish the Wayland socket and start the backend
allocate Xwayland and export WAYLAND_DISPLAY and DISPLAY
startup.startup_command_role: best-effort child, never the compositor supervisor
startup.startup_command_failure: report through child status/logging without ending the compositor
startup.validation_failure: exit nonzero before sockets, backend start, Xwayland, or startup command
startup.runtime_initialization_failure: tear down all initialized resources and exit nonzero before startup command

logout.cleanup: destroy compositor-owned resources and disconnect native Wayland and Xwayland clients

failure_recovery.crash_recovery: the launcher returns the child failure; a later independent login starts from the last complete explicit save

state_file.missing_file: successful empty state with root focus
state_file.malformed_or_unsupported_file: diagnose, retain the file byte-for-byte, and start clean
state_file.save: mode-0600 same-directory temporary file, flush, fsync, close, atomic rename
state_file.lifetime: persistent until an explicit successful replacement or user removal

requirements.rule: wtwm-session runs exactly one foreground compositor child, never loops or replaces the display manager, and returns the child status.
Configuration validation completes before runtime resources and the optional startup command; the command runs only after the Wayland and Xwayland environment is published.
Invalid configuration or runtime initialization exits nonzero, does not execute the startup command, and leaves any saved state unchanged.
f.quit terminates the event loop, performs complete compositor cleanup, disconnects both protocol families, and exits successfully.
SIGINT, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT, and SIGTERM enter the same orderly successful cleanup boundary as f.quit.
Failure of the optional startup command does not terminate or restart the compositor.
The launcher never automatically restarts a cleanly exited or failed compositor; the login manager owns the next login attempt.
Only f.saveyourself replaces the persistent compositor state; logout, signals, startup failures, and crashes never perform an implicit save.
Missing state starts empty, while malformed or unsupported state is diagnosed and ignored without modifying the file or preventing startup.
wtwm does not implement XSM -clientId/-restore restart commands or discard callbacks; its explicit persistent state restores only compositor-owned state.

verification_scenarios.oracle: Exit 2 before runtime initialization or startup command.
Exit 1 with no socket, Xwayland, startup command, or state-file mutation.
Exit 1 after bounded teardown with no startup command or state-file mutation.
The command observes the new WAYLAND_DISPLAY and DISPLAY values.
A nonzero startup child does not end the live compositor.
Both clients are live before f.quit, then disconnect during complete cleanup and the compositor exits 0.
SIGINT produces complete cleanup and exit 0.
SIGHUP produces complete cleanup and exit 0.
SIGQUIT produces complete cleanup and exit 0.
SIGTERM produces complete cleanup and exit 0.
A controlling signal is forwarded as TERM, the child is reaped exactly once, and its final status is returned.
A failed child status is logged and returned without another launch.
RestartPreviousState starts with empty root-focused state and does not create a file.
Startup diagnoses the file, starts clean, and leaves its bytes unchanged through logout.
The previous complete state remains byte-identical and no temporary file remains.
f.quit and every orderly signal leave the persistent state path absent or byte-identical.
The launcher returns the failure and a separate later invocation can start normally from the last complete explicit state.

deferred: XSM or D-Bus session-manager protocol emulation
